statement: The American regional Mexican band Grupo Frontera was involved in a controversy due to an alleged endorsement of the politician and current United States president Donald Trump since early 2025.
The controversy began after a video of one of Grupo Frontera's vocalists' relatives performing a 'Trump dance' to the Village People's 'Y.M.C.A.' went viral.
Despite answers in an interview with El País, fans interpreted the video as an endorsement of Trump from Grupo Frontera.
Fans later allegedly discovered videos containing support for Trump and a deleted TikTok of Grupo Frontera dancing to the same song.
Users considered the discovered videos and deleted TikTok clear evidence of the accusations against Grupo Frontera.
Users started to cancel and boycott Grupo Frontera on social media.
Users called Grupo Frontera 'traitors'.
Users asked for a cancellation of one of Grupo Frontera's festival performances through Change.org.
Grupo Frontera responded twice to the controversy in February 2025 through Instagram.
Grupo Frontera denied any endorsement of Donald Trump in their Instagram responses.
Grupo Frontera responded to other accusations in their Instagram statements.
Grupo Frontera confirmed their support of the Mexican community in their Instagram declarations.
Grupo Frontera's declarations received mainly negative reactions from the public.
The public argued that Grupo Frontera's declarations were only an attempt to maintain the group's reputation among fans.
The controversy also received attention from Pepe Aguilar's sons, Emiliano and Leonardo Aguilar.
The controversy received attention from online media.
An interview with Grupo Frontera by Raúl Novoa in Madrid about their career achievements and experiences was published through El País on January 5, 2025.

For the question about the candidate Donald Trump's re-election as the US president, Juan Javier Cantú answered: 'We rarely get involved in politics. It's very controversial for us and we just want to make music.'
Juan Javier Cantú and Alberto 'Beto' Acosta highlighted their donation of toys for children to a community centre for immigrants that were deported by the border policies.
Regarding the Mexico–United States wall, Alberto 'Beto' Acosta shared Grupo Frontera's disagreement.
Julián Peña Jr. opined about the inconclusion of the Mexico–United States wall.
Later that month, a video went viral on social media.

The viral video showed Grupo Frontera's vocalist Adelaido 'Payo' Solís' grandmother, alias 'La Abuela Frontera', dancing in a similar way to Trump to the Village People's 'Y.M.C.A.' with other relatives.
The song 'Y.M.C.A.' was used by Donald Trump for his 2024 presidential campaign.
The viral video caused outrage among Grupo Frontera's fans on social media.
Critics called for Grupo Frontera's cancellation due to the viral video.
The 'La Abuela Frontera' account disappeared on TikTok.

During the period in which the video was going viral, a user on TikTok named Sarah Jasmine claimed that Grupo Frontera deleted videos in which they had explicitly endorsed Donald Trump and sympathized with his politics.
As a result of the controversy, Grupo Frontera received a significant drop in followers.
Grupo Frontera received an influx of hate comments.
Grupo Frontera received accusations of being Latinos for Trump and betraying their core audience.
Fans called for Grupo Frontera to be canceled.
Fans called for Grupo Frontera's presence to be rejected in Mexico.
Fans called for others to refrain from consuming any content related to Grupo Frontera, including songs, videos and live performances.
Videos of booing at one of Grupo Frontera's recent concerts circulated online.
Screencasts showing the personal Instagram accounts of some Grupo Frontera members following Trump's profile and liking his posts also circulated online.
Some users noticed that Grupo Frontera deleted a TikTok video dancing to the same song as Solís' grandmother.
Users considered the deleted TikTok video explicit evidence of an endorsement.

On February 11, a petition on the American website Change.org was published by alias 'Espíritu' to cancel Grupo Frontera's participation at the 2025 edition of the Chicago Latin music festival Sueños.
The petition accumulated over 9,700 signatures the next day.
Sueños co-founder Christopher Den Uijl affirmed on Instagram the festival's support to the Latino community.
Christopher Den Uijl stated that none of the Sueños co-founders are supporters of the president.
Christopher Den Uijl did not mention anything related to Grupo Frontera in his statement.
After a few weeks without communication on the subject, Grupo Frontera published a video of a US crowd singing 'Bebé Dame'.
Media described the video of the US crowd singing 'Bebé Dame' as an indirect response to the controversy.
On February 7, Grupo Frontera published a statement through Instagram stories.
In their Instagram statement, Grupo Frontera argued that they do not have 'affiliation nor alliance with any political party that [is] against immigrants and the Latino community'.
Grupo Frontera clarified that they and their families are immigrants and come from the frontier.
Grupo Frontera clarified their support to Mexicans.
Grupo Frontera clarified that 'opinions of [their] friends and family [do not] represent [the band]'.
In an interview with Jesse Cervantes for EXA FM, Grupo Frontera affirmed their commitment to the immigrant community.
In an interview with Jesse Cervantes for EXA FM, Grupo Frontera affirmed their pride in Mexican culture, 'without distinction of ideologies and borders'.
On the 37th Lo Nuestro Awards' red carpet, the Cuban-American television presenter Raúl de Molina asked Grupo Frontera about the controversy.
Raúl de Molina's question visibly made Grupo Frontera appear uncomfortable.
Julián Peña Jr.'s response to the question was: 'We dedicate ourselves to music. We love everyone and want peace and love. Take care of yourselves'.
Peña's response was called 'poor'.
Peña's response was linked by fans to the rumors of Grupo Frontera's support of Trump.
On February 22, Grupo Frontera published a video on Instagram affirming their previous statement.
In the February 22 video, Alberto 'Beto' Acosta said that their silence was for the huge amount of 'fake news' spread on the Internet.
Acosta stated that they did not know how to answer due to the 'fake news'.
Grupo Frontera clarified that the dance video was only a backstage routine during their past concert tour, Jugando a Que No Pasa Nada Tour.
During the Jugando a Que No Pasa Nada Tour, Grupo Frontera danced to songs from their primary school period.
Other fans reacted against the massive cancellation of Grupo Frontera.
Other fans supported Grupo Frontera's freedom of speech.
According to Infobae Mexico's Víctor Cisneros, fans argued that 'cancel culture should not spread to those with different political opinions'.
Juan Garza of Periódico ABC praised the way that Grupo Frontera managed the controversy.
Juan Garza spoke against the backlash Grupo Frontera received.
Juan Garza claimed that in many cases in the entertainment world the information spread on social media linking public figures to politicians was 'erroneous'.
Both the public and some online newspapers labeled the concert booing as fake with altered audio.
'Espíritu' admitted that the TikTok dance video did not amount to an explicit endorsement.
'Espíritu' said the TikTok dance video was strategically implicit.
Chicago Sun-Times's staff opined that '[Donald Trump] and [Grupo Frontera] [...] [could] simply have similar tastes in music'.
The February 7 statement polarized fans' opinions.
Some fans applauded the February 7 statement.
Other fans argued that the February 7 statement was not authentic and was only an attempt to maintain Grupo Frontera's reputation among fans.
A representative of Grupo Frontera confirmed the authenticity of the February 7 statement.
The February 22 video received negative reactions from users.
Users accused the February 22 video of the same issues as the statement.
Users complained that Grupo Frontera never directly rejected Trump in the February 22 video.
Rolling Stone's Tomás Mier also noticed that Grupo Frontera never directly rejected Trump in the February 22 video.
Leonelys Gomez of the Latin Times named the controversy as one of Grupo Frontera's biggest during their three-year career.
Marca's staff linked the controversy with Banda MS and Fuerza Regida's situation.
Marca's staff emphasized the personal opinions of some members of Banda MS and Fuerza Regida.
Many fans compared the controversy with the Yahritza y su Esencia's 2023 backlash.
Yahritza y su Esencia's 2023 backlash occurred when they visited Mexico.
During the 2023 backlash, vocalist Yahritza Martinez confessed controversial preferences, despising Mexico and Mexican cuisine.
After the 2023 backlash, Yahritza y su Esencia stopped performing in Mexico.
Pepe Aguilar's son, Emiliano Aguilar, reacted through a series of Instagram stories in favor of the cancellation of Grupo Frontera.
Emiliano Aguilar said, 'Fuck [Grupo Frontera]. Mexico must be respected'.
Emiliano Aguilar's reaction came after releasing 'Ilegal', a protest song against Trump's mass deportation.
'Ilegal' received public acclaim and support from deported immigrants.
Emiliano Aguilar's half-brother, Leonardo, expressed his support to Grupo Frontera after they published the video.
Leonardo Aguilar wrote in the post comments, '[Do not worry]. We the fans [will still supporting you]. The rest are people without anything to do. [We] know who you are'.
Emiliano Aguilar has conflicts with his family.
Emiliano Aguilar commented on the same video with many Mexican flags.
Emiliano Aguilar answered Leonardo, saying: 'Grupo 'Frontera', I could not care less. Pure Mexico'.
After that, Emiliano Aguilar published another series of Instagram stories repeating his hatred of Grupo Frontera.
Emiliano Aguilar referred to his brother Leonardo as 'Gallito Fino'.
Emiliano Aguilar related Leonardo's sympathy with an indifference to the immigrant community.
Emiliano Aguilar argued, 'Here is a Mexican who dies for his people with firmness in his conviction. [...] You have always had everything, you have never lacked attention and love from the public'.
Emiliano Aguilar finished saying that he and Leonardo had talked about the problem civilly in private.
Emiliano Aguilar stated that Leonardo worsened the situation because '[he] already [roared]'.
According to La Razón's Mariana Garibay, the public complained that Emiliano Aguilar may have been looking for controversies only in order to catch attention.
